transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-07-22
Time: 14:30 - 15:22 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Rafael Ortiz, Priya Nair (Redwood) | Tom Bennett, Lina Park, Arjun Mehta, Sofia Ruiz (CruxForge)

Auto-generated summary (may be incomplete):
- Intro + mutual context: CruxForge is evaluating hybrid GPU partner to offload inference for an internal ML platform.
- Primary concerns: latency SLOs for real-time features, data residency, key management, cost per token and reserved capacity options.
- Agreed next steps: share sizing worksheet, pilot pricing, schedule on-prem micro-benchmark.

Topics: hybrid deployment, VPC/private deployment, GPU availability, SOC2/KMS, benchmarks, pilot scope

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, um, appreciate it. Quick round-robin, I'll be Maya, AE working with partners. Rafael's our SE for infra and performance. Priya's on the integration side.
[00:22] Tom (CruxForge CTO): Hi, I'm Tom, CTO at CruxForge. Lina is our infra head, Arjun runs security and Sofia does ML infra. Thanks, Maya.
[00:37] Lina (CruxForge): Hey, quick note — we're on a tight timeline, Q3 pilot goal.
[00:44] Rafael (Redwood SE): Awesome, yeah that's helpful. Real quick, can you give a short snapshot of current stack and where you want Redwood to sit?
[00:56] Sofia (CruxForge): Sure — we run a mix of cloud-hosted services (multi-AZ) and some on-prem racks for sensitive workloads. Model inference today is in-house on NVMe attached servers, but we see spikes and we want a partner to handle large-batch and realtime low-latency endpoints. Preference for hybrid — hosted for non-prod and on-prem or VPC peered for prod.
[01:18] Priya (Redwood): Got it. When you say realtime low-latency, what's the p50/p95 targets?
[01:25] Sofia (CruxForge): p50 ~60-80ms, p95 under 200ms for short-context chat interactions — 1k token windows typical. But for larger batch scoring it's okay to be in 300-600ms range.
[01:41] Rafael (Redwood SE): Ok that's helpful. A couple of flags — that p95 under 200ms for 1k tokens is tight, depends on model and quantization. We often recommend-- um-- either a dedicated pool or VPC private nodes for predictable SLOs.
[02:00] Tom (CruxForge): Yeah, why would dedicated be better vs hosted? Cost tradeoffs?
[02:07] Maya (Redwood AE): Great question — dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity so bursty spikes don't throttle you; hosted is cheaper and faster to start but you can see higher variance. For strict latency SLOs, dedicated or private deployment (Redwood Private) is common.
[02:25] Arjun (Security): On the security side, we need SOC2 Type II, KMS integration for customer-managed keys, audit logs at token level, and SSO/SAML. Also data residency in EU for some customers. Do you support those?
[02:40] Priya (Redwood): Yes, Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM and we can plug in customer-managed keys via our control plane. We maintain audit logs and SSO with SAML/SCIM. SOC2 attestation is in the security pack — we'll share that.
[02:56] Lina (CruxForge): And what about air-gapped/on-prem installs?
[03:01] Rafael (Redwood SE): We have an on-prem option, yeah. It's not a simple drop-in but we can run a private control plane with your network. Some customers do a thin data-plane inside the VPC and control plane outside — that reduces maintenance.
[03:16] Tom (CruxForge CTO): Interesting. For licensing and pricing, do you do reserved monthly capacity? We have predictable nightly batches.
[03:25] Maya (Redwood AE): Yes, Redwood Dedicated has reserved capacity contracts, monthly or annual. For mixed workloads you can do a baseline reserved pool plus burst capacity. We'll send a GPU sizing worksheet to map your nightly batch vs realtime needs.
[03:40] [00:04:00] Sofia (CruxForge): Quick, um, what's the typical on-prem footprint for a small pilot? Two nodes? Four?
[03:48] Rafael (Redwood SE): For a pilot, 2x A100-class or equivalent (or a mix with 80GB and 40GB) is typical depending on model. If you're using quantized Llama-family models you can do more with less.
[04:05] Maya (Redwood AE): We'll include an example pilot configuration in the worksheet.
[04:10] [00:06:00] Tom (CruxForge): About model compatibility — we use a mix of open models and some internally fine-tuned checkpoints. Can Redwood run custom checkpoints?
[04:21] Priya (Redwood): Yes, we onboard customer weights; there are some constraints depending on model architecture and licensing. Also kernel selection for attention patterns can affect perf — we'll do a compat scan.
[04:36] Arjun (Security): Are customer weights encrypted at rest? Who manages keys?
[04:41] Priya (Redwood): Yes, encrypted. Optionally you can manage keys via your KMS (bring-your-own-key). For private deployments keys can stay in your HSM.
[04:52] [00:08:00] Lina (CruxForge): Data residency — we need EU-only for certain tenants. Can we force routing?
[05:00] Rafael (Redwood SE): Yes, routing policies can pin requests to regionally isolated pools. There is also fallback logic if capacity is exhausted but that can be disabled for compliance-critical flows.
[05:14] Sofia (CruxForge): What about prefix KV caching? We have lots of repeated context.
[05:20] Rafael (Redwood SE): Redwood runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching which reduces per-token cost and latency for repeated contexts — we'll show cache hit expectations in the benchmark.
[05:31] [00:10:00] Tom (CruxForge CTO): Another question: we've heard about some providers having noisy neighbors on shared GPUs. How do you isolate?
[05:39] Rafael (Redwood SE): For hosted, yes you can see interference; dedicated pools and private nodes isolate you. We also have scheduling policies to prioritize latency vs throughput.
[05:52] Maya (Redwood AE): Also note we can route critical traffic to dedicated and fallback to hosted for cost-sensitive tasks.
[05:59] [00:12:00] Arjun (Security): Compliance checks — can we get pen-test reports, and do you do regular third-party audits?
[06:08] Priya (Redwood): We have SOC2 Type II, and we run third-party pentests — we'll add the last pen-test summary to the security deck.
[06:17] Lina (CruxForge): Will you provide an SLA for latency?
[06:21] Rafael (Redwood SE): SLAs are throughput/availability based primarily; latency SLOs are included in dedicated contracts as targets and we have tracing and per-route dashboards to measure. Absolute SLO guarantees can be included in enterprise agreements.
[06:36] [00:15:00] Sofia (CruxForge): On the pilot, we'd like a simple success criteria: 95th percentile latency under 200ms for chat endpoint and cost per 1k tokens below our in-house baseline. Will Redwood help instrument cost tracking?
[06:52] Maya (Redwood AE): Yes — Redwood Console shows token-level cost, per-route breakdowns, and you can tag routes for cost tracking. We'll help instrument with SDK hooks during the pilot.
[07:04] Tom (CruxForge): Is streaming supported for partial responses? Our app uses streaming tokens for UX.
[07:10] Priya (Redwood): Streaming responses and function/tool calling are supported in the hosted and dedicated runtimes. On private, we can enable the same APIs.
[07:20] [00:18:00] Lina (CruxForge): Ok, I'd like to understand fallback policies — if the dedicated pool is full, do requests go to hosted automatically? That would be bad for compliance.
[07:29] Rafael (Redwood SE): There are configurable fallback policies. For compliance-critical tenants we can disable fallback. For others we can allow fallback with warnings.
[07:40] Arjun (Security): Do you store logs with PII?
[07:44] Priya (Redwood): By default logs are anonymized and we can configure retention and redaction. You can opt to never persist raw inputs on private infra.
[07:55] [00:20:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Quick product note — some customers call our Dedicated "Redwood Devoted" in docs, so you may see different phrasing, ignore the typo in older slides.
[08:06] Tom (CruxForge): (laughs) ok no worries.
[08:10] Sofia (CruxForge): Can we run our own quantization? We have a pipeline that quantizes to int8.
[08:15] Rafael (Redwood SE): You can bring quantized models but we recommend we handle quantization optimally in the runtime — container-level differences can affect perf. We can test both.
[08:27] [00:23:00] Priya (Redwood): For the benchmark plan we typically do: small-scale latency p95 test, throughput ramp, and a KV cache hit-rate simulation. We'll provide scripts. We prefer a shared runner in your network or an SSH runner you allow for transient tests.
[08:44] Tom (CruxForge CTO): SSH runner sounds fine. Security team will vet it.
[08:48] Arjun (Security): We'll need a network diagram and firewall rules for the runner. Also access policy and temporary keys.
[08:57] Maya (Redwood AE): We'll include a sample network diagram in the pack.
[09:02] [00:26:00] Lina (CruxForge): There's a procurement question: our finance needs an estimate for both pilot and a 6-month committed plan. When can we get draft pricing?
[09:12] Maya (Redwood AE): We'll share pilot pricing and a model for reserved vs burst pricing. Expect a draft by EOD 2025-07-25.
[09:20] [00:28:00] Sofia (CruxForge): Any references for similar customers doing hybrid? We want to see one pager.
[09:26] Priya (Redwood): Yes, we'll send a short case study (anonymized) and a partner reference.
[09:33] Rafael (Redwood SE): Also, note the kernel selection matters for long-context models — we'll do an eval to pick optimized kernels.
[09:40] Tom (CruxForge): On token accounting — does Redwood charge for generated tokens only or both prompt+completion?
[09:46] Maya (Redwood AE): We charge per input+output token units; pricing sheet will show examples and the effect of caching.
[09:53] [00:31:00] Arjun (Security): For the SOC2 docs, can we get redacted logs and controls matrix?
[09:59] Priya (Redwood): Yes, we'll include a controls matrix and a redacted log sample.
[10:06] Lina (CruxForge): If we go private, what's the uplift for on-prem vs hosted? Ballpark percentage?
[10:12] Rafael (Redwood SE): On-prem has infra and support premiums; ballpark is 20-40% uplift depending on scale and support SLA. We'll put ranges in the draft pricing.
[10:24] [00:34:00] Sofia (CruxForge): Ok timeline alignment: we want a pilot in August and production by October if pilot passes. Is that feasible?
[10:33] Maya (Redwood AE): Yes that's reasonable. Pilot in August, iterative bench, then production ramp in September/October. We'll coordinate resources.
[10:42] Tom (CruxForge): Anything around model-rotation or version pinning? We want to pin model versions for regressions.
[10:48] Priya (Redwood): You can pin model versions and use rollout policies for canary and A/B tests. We also support automatic fallback to a previous pinned version.
[10:59] [00:36:00] Rafael (Redwood SE): For the micro-benchmark we'll need sample payloads and a distribution of sequence lengths. If you share those, we'll tune batching and kernel choices.
[11:08] Sofia (CruxForge): We'll extract three representative workloads and upload them to the shared folder.
[11:14] Arjun (Security): One more on encryption — transit TLS mutual?
[11:18] Priya (Redwood): Mutual TLS can be used between our control plane and on-prem nodes. We'll include that in the network doc.
[11:26] [00:40:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Great — I'm going to recap: Redwood to send partner intro deck, security pack (SOC2, pen-test summary, KMS docs), GPU sizing worksheet, pilot pricing draft. CruxForge to share throughput profile, sample payloads, access window for micro-bench and procurement constraints.
[11:45] Tom (CruxForge CTO): Sounds good. Also note that our procurement needs an MSA template and insurance requirements early.
[11:52] Maya (Redwood AE): We'll attach a redlined sample MSA and insurance checklist.
[11:57] [00:44:00] Lina (CruxForge): Ok any hidden gotchas? Latency can spike under certain kernel combos?
[12:03] Rafael (Redwood SE): Yeah algorithmic changes or attention kernels differ — that's why we run the compatibility scan. Sometimes naming in transcriptions shows "Redwood Devoted" instead of Dedicated, bit of a legacy doc typo — not a functional difference.
[12:18] Sofia (CruxForge): (laughs) noted.
[12:22] [00:47:00] Maya (Redwood AE): We'll send links after the call: partner-deck.pdf (link), security-pack.zip (link), gpu-sizing.xlsx (link), benchmark-scripts repo (link).
[12:34] Tom (CruxForge): Perfect, thanks. If pilot pricing looks good procurement will move fast.
[12:40] Priya (Redwood): We'll be ready to support the micro-benchmark and can join the initial integration sync.
[12:47] Arjun (Security): We'll schedule a security review with your team next week.
[12:51] Maya (Redwood AE): Great — last thing, is there anyone else we should loop in?
[12:56] Tom (CruxForge CTO): Maybe our legal lead and cloud ops manager — I'll send contact.
[13:02] Maya (Redwood AE): Awesome. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the pack by tomorrow.

--- End transcript ---
